Alternate method: If one studying the scientific question and one executing the laser microdissection are separate personnel, working at separate places/time zones, a crude method to designate the region of interest can be followed: Image the Nissl-stained forebrain sections mounted on the regular plus slides, 1 for every 10 sections mounted on PEN slides. Copy and paste each image as a separate slide in Microsoft PowerPoint. Carefully trace the region of interest, using PowerPoint tools, as shown in Figure 3D . steps.title: Prepare RNase‑free work area
steps.instruction: Wear sterile disposable gloves and change them frequently. Autoclave dissection instruments and spatula, then wipe with RNaseZap, rinse with RNase‑free DNase‑free water and dry with Kimwipes. Clean the dissection surface with 100 % RNaseZap solution and let dry. Label embedding molds with a Fisherbrand permanent marker on the side opposite the notch. Gather all reagents, ice bucket, dry‑ice, and a clean 5‑slide mailer with desiccant.

steps.title: Prepare OCT embedding molds
steps.instruction: Crush dry‑ice with a mallet to create a soft powdered bed. Place a sterile embedding mold (Thermo Scientific, cat 70182) on the powdered dry‑ice. Slowly pour Optimum Cutting Temperature (OCT) embedding compound (Electron Microscopy Sciences, cat 62550‑01) along one edge of the mold until it is half‑filled, avoiding air bubbles.

steps.title: Euthanize neonatal pups
steps.instruction: Place P0‑P6 mouse pups on the lid of a sterile 100 mm Petri dish (Fisher, cat FB0875713) atop crushed ice for 2–3 min until unconscious (no response to firm toe pinch). Decapitate with sharp scissors. Transfer heads to a new sterile 100 mm Petri dish containing sterile 1× PBS (Gibco, cat 10010‑023).

substeps.instruction: If genotyping is required, cut ≤ 2 mm of tail and place in a labeled 1.7 ml RNase‑free tube (Olympus/Genesee, cat 24‑282A).
Dispose of carcasses in labeled small biohazard bags (Medline, cat DYND30261).

steps.title: Dissect forebrain
steps.instruction: Under a dissection microscope, use fine and coarse forceps to remove the brain from PBS. If the PBS becomes blood‑stained, transfer brains to a fresh dish of sterile PBS. Trim away hindbrain and midbrain, retaining the forebrain with olfactory bulbs for orientation.

steps.title: Embed brain in OCT
steps.instruction: Using a spatula and coarse forceps, place the forebrain into the half‑filled OCT mold. Blot excess surface liquid with a finely rolled Kimwipe if needed. Orient the brain so the anterior (olfactory‑bulb) side is perpendicular to the notched side of the mold for coronal sections. Slowly add OCT to fully cover the brain, avoiding bubbles. Place the mold on powdered dry‑ice, supporting the sides with more dry‑ice, until the OCT becomes opaque. Transfer the frozen block to a clean 2‑inch cryogenic freezer box and store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Prepare cryostat and slides
steps.instruction: Clean the cryostat, microtome blade, and tools with a 1:1 mixture of RNaseZap and 70 % ethanol (Recipe 1), then with sterile 95 % ethanol (Recipe 3); dry with Kimwipes. Incubate PEN‑membrane slides (Leica, cat 11505189) under UV light for 30 min. Prepare fresh 75 % ethanol (Recipe 4) and Nissl stain (Recipe 5) at least 3 days before use and store at 4 °C. Set cryostat temperature to –15 °C to –18 °C. Label each PEN slide with brain code/genotype using a pencil.

steps.title: Cryo‑section forebrain
steps.instruction: Transfer the frozen OCT block from –80 °C to the cryostat using new sterile single‑edge blades. Trim the block as needed. Attach the block to the chuck so the anterior (notched) side faces perpendicular to the blade. Allow the block to equilibrate on the cryostat for ≥ 20 min. Cut 8–10 µm sections and mount them on regular charged slides; quickly Nissl‑stain (≈ 1 min) to locate the region of interest (ROI). Once ROI is identified, cut 16–18 µm sections and mount them on PEN slides (≈ 12–14 sections per slide). Collect one of every 5–10 sections on a regular slide for histology. Air‑dry PEN slides on desiccant for ~2 min at room temperature. Clean the blade and stage with a brush or Kimwipe between sections.

steps.title: Dehydrate and Nissl‑stain PEN slides
steps.instruction: Place each PEN slide (or batch) in a 50 ml tube. Immerse slides in fresh 100 % ethanol for 5 min, repeat 4 times on a rocking shaker to remove OCT. Transfer to freshly prepared 75 % ethanol for ~1 min. Apply 10–15 drops of Nissl stain directly onto each section using a plastic transfer pipette; incubate 1 min, then gently swivel the slide. Rinse quickly with fresh 100 % ethanol for 5 s, repeat 3 times. Finish with a final 1 min immersion in fresh 100 % ethanol. Observe under a bright‑field dissecting microscope, then let slides dry for ≥ 30 min (or ≥ 10 min total staining time). Store completely dried slides either at –80 °C in a vacuum‑sealed mailer with desiccant or proceed immediately to LCM.

steps.title: Prepare for laser microdissection
steps.instruction: Remove PEN slides from –80 °C and let them equilibrate to room temperature for ≥ 60 min (or dry in a desiccator). Switch on the Leica LMD system. Clean 0.5 ml collection tube caps (Thermowell, cat 6530) with RNaseZap, rinse with RNase‑free water, and dry. Add 20–40 µl of RLT buffer (Qiagen RNeasy Plus Micro Kit) containing 10 µl 2‑mercaptoethanol per 1 ml RLT (final 1 % v/v) to each cap. Set LMD software to transmitted‑light bright‑field mode, use “Close line” drawing, “Move + Cut” mode, and “Fine” X‑Y‑Z precision. Load PEN slides upside‑down in the stack‑slide holder and create a low‑magnification (1.25×) overview.

steps.title: Laser‑capture microdissection
steps.instruction: Trace the ROI on the slide (using prior Nissl‑stained regular slides or PowerPoint tracings if performed by a separate person). Cut the ROI on the PEN slide; tissue will fall by gravity into the prepared collection tube cap. Load a new collection tube every 2 h if cutting takes longer. After completing a slide, repeat for subsequent slides. Store used slides for later inspection if desired. If multiple cell types are needed, collect each type into separate tubes, using different holes in the tube holder to avoid cross‑contamination. Unfinished PEN slides may be kept in a desiccator with desiccant at room temperature for up to 5 days.

steps.title: Recover and store microdissected material
steps.instruction: After cutting, close each collection tube cap upside‑down, vortex for 1 min, then briefly centrifuge to collect the lysate at the bottom. Store tubes at –80 °C until RNA extraction.

steps.title: Isolate RNA from LCM samples
steps.instruction: Pool all RLT‑buffer lysates of the same genotype/replicate into a new RNase‑free 1.7 ml tube. Vortex 30 s. Add an equal volume of RNase‑free 70 % ethanol (Recipe 2). If the total volume exceeds 700 µl, load ≤ 700 µl onto an RNeasy MinElute spin column (Qiagen) and repeat until the entire mixture is processed. Follow the RNeasy Plus Micro Kit manual to wash and elute RNA with 15 µl RNase‑free water containing RNase inhibitor (1 U/µl). Take 2 µl of eluate, dilute with 2–3 µl RNase‑free water, and measure concentration and purity on a NanoDrop. Optionally split each sample into three technical replicates for downstream applications (e.g., RNA‑seq).

steps.title: Prepare ethanol solutions (Recipes)
steps.instruction: Use RNase‑free molecular‑grade water for all recipes. 70 % ethanol: mix 70 ml RNase‑free absolute ethanol with 30 ml water (store –20 °C). 95 % ethanol: mix 95 ml RNase‑free absolute ethanol with 5 ml water (store –20 °C). RNaseZap/70 % ethanol (1:1, 100 ml): combine 50 ml RNaseZap (Invitrogen, cat AM9780) with 50 ml 70 % ethanol; rock 4–5 min, use to clean cryostat and tools. 75 % ethanol (fresh): mix 75 ml RNase‑free absolute ethanol with 25 ml water (store –20 °C).

steps.title: Prepare Nissl stain (Recipe)
steps.instruction: Weigh 0.5 g cresyl violet powder into a RNase‑free 50 ml tube. Add RNase‑free absolute ethanol to a final concentration of 1 % w/v (≈ 50 ml). Shake for several hours, then store sealed, dark at 4 °C for up to 6 months. Prepare at least 3 days before use and aliquot as needed.
